messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: high 5xx/error rate on /v1/generate across eu-west and us-west clusters (alert id 8472)
pagerduty: Channel: #incidents, Severity: P1 - paging on-call
alex: I'm on it, grabbing the on-call handoff. seeing ~40% 5xx increase, latency spiking, some 502s.
maya: seeing pod restarts in runtime-gpu pool, crashloops on several replicas. CUDA errors in logs (cuMemcpyKind mismatch) and OOMs.
leo: autoscaler log shows repeated scale-up then immediate scale-down in last 8m — looks like snapback oscillation. pools: gpu-preemptible + dedicated.
katie: customers reporting degraded response times and partial failures, some LLM requests failing early. opening broadcast to cs.
sre_jordan: tagging for handoff @alex @maya. what's current mitigation?
alex: initial mitigation: disabled new deployments, set route fallback to smaller CPU-optimized model for non-critical tenants.
maya: stack trace sample from pod-rt-57:
```
RuntimeError: Cuda error: out of memory when allocating 1.2GiB
  at inference_runner.py:142
  at kv_cache.py:88
```
leo: also seeing kube events: node eviction spikes after scale-in; pods being rescheduled nonstop -> cold-start kernel/driver reinit, failing on CUDA init sometimes.
alex: hypothesis: aggressive autoscaler (scaleDown.delay=30s, scaleUp.threshold low) spins up many preemptible GPUs, they get preempted or fail init -> autoscaler sees low capacity usage and tears down -> loop. combination with prefix cache misses causes OOMs on init.
katie: CS update: several enterprise customers affected (ids redacted). CS sent temporary workarounds. Need ETA for stable service.
sre_jordan: mitigation plan I propose:
- pause autoscaler scale-down / increase cooldown to 10m on runtime pools
- temporarily remove preemptible GPU pool from autoscaling target
- manually cordon a set of healthy GPU nodes and create a reserved capacity group (3 nodes)
- roll restart runtime pods that are crashlooping after cordon
- revert routing to primary after verifying stability
Any objections?
maya: +1. Also add: increase pod memory reservation to avoid OOM at init (temp safety margin) and disable continuous batching for a few minutes to reduce peak memory.
leo: I'll run the kubectl/drain/cordon steps. commands I will run:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-12 && kubectl label node gpu-node-12 reserved=true
kubectl scale deployment/runtime-gpu --replicas=0 --namespace=prod
# after cordon and node ready
kubectl scale deployment/runtime-gpu --replicas=6 --namespace=prod
```

Note: adjusting autoscaler config in cloud console (will require a 90s deploy).
alex: I'll patch the autoscaler: set scaleDownUnneededTime=600, scaleDownDelay=600, remove preemptible pool from target. also temporarily increase minReplicas to 6.
devopsbot: Applying autoscaler patch (change set queued).
leo: drained 2 nodes, marked reserved nodes, spinning up reserved replicas. seeing GPU drivers load cleanly.
maya: after reserved nodes come up, crashloops reduce. still seeing a couple CUDA init failures on older nodes; evicting old nodes.
katie: CS update sent: "We are actively mitigating; some requests may be slower. Team will follow up with rollback/patch ETA." :white_check_mark:
sre_jordan: monitoring: error rate dropping from +40% to +8% over last 6 minutes, p50 latency normalizing.
alex: routing back to primary models in 15 min if stable, otherwise keep fallback.
leo: note: discovered autoscaler pod logs show a bug where scale-in metric considered CPU-only, ignoring queued GPU-backed pods — filed issue INFRA-348.
maya: created hotfix PR to increase init-time memory reservation and add retry on CUDA init.

---

Post-incident immediate actions to capture (for handoff):
- owners: alex (oncall lead), maya (runtime), leo (infra)
- immediate mitigations applied: autoscaler cooldown increase, preemptible pool excluded, reserved node group created, roll restarts done, temporary memory bump, batching disabled
- customer impact: elevated 5xx and latency for ~22 minutes, partial failures for some enterprise tenants, fallback to CPU model reduced impact for most traffic
- next steps before postmortem: collect kernel/gpu-driver logs, autoscaler metric dumps, node lifecycle events, list of affected customers, timeline of autoscaler actions and preemption events
- follow-ups: INFRA-348 autoscaler metric bug, runtime init OOM hardening, autoscaler safety gating to avoid oscillation, better canary for preemptible pools

sre_jordan: I'll create the incident ticket and schedule postmortem. tagging this thread for handoff.
alex: thanks team — will stay on until we see stable metrics for 30m then hand off to follow-up owners. :heart
